title: Inequality & Policy: Final Assessment
description: A final assessment covering the key ideas from all three lessons. Reach the passing score to complete the course.

history.note: AI-written question draft. Not yet reviewed by a human (admin); do not give to students.

Comprehensive audit: q1 states Jamal's assets; q3 names the n-squared convention; q9 assumption moved into the prompt so the key is not the only hedged choice, retagged intermediate; q7 distractors made plausible; q10 stem no longer echoes the key; q9 sales-tax explanation conditional; independent AI review follow-ups. Lead QA: q3 prompt says compute exactly, then round. Not reviewed or approved by a human.

passing.note: Proposed: 7 of 10 questions (70%). Not approved by a teacher (admin); completion is not recognized until approved.

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Rosa is retired, has a small pension, and owns a paid-off house worth $400,000. Jamal is 25, earns $70,000 a year, owes $30,000 in student loans, and has almost no savings or other assets. Which description fits?

choices.text: Rosa has low income but high wealth; Jamal has higher income but little wealth
Rosa has high income and high wealth; Jamal has low income and low wealth
Rosa and Jamal have similar wealth, because wealth counts yearly earnings
Jamal has more wealth, because his yearly pay is larger than his debt

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Country R's cumulative income shares for the poorest 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% are 6%, 16%, 32%, and 56%. Country S's are 4%, 14%, 34%, and 60%. What can you conclude from the Lorenz curves alone?

choices.text: Country R is more equal, because its poorest quintile has a larger share
Country S is more equal, because its bottom 80% has a larger share
The curves cross, so the Lorenz curves alone cannot rank the countries
The countries are equally unequal, because both curves end at 100%

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: Four roommates have monthly incomes of $1,000, $2,000, $3,000, and $6,000. Using the course's population formula G = Σᵢ Σⱼ |yᵢ − yⱼ| ÷ (2n²μ) over all ordered pairs, compute the Gini coefficient exactly, then round it. (Enter a decimal rounded to two decimal places, with no unit.)
Hypothetical example: An income tax charges 20% on income up to $50,000 and 35% on income above $50,000. Ana gets a raise from $49,000 to $52,000. What happens?

choices.text: Her whole income is now taxed at 35%, so her after-tax income falls
The $2,000 above $50,000 is taxed at 35%, so her after-tax income rises
Her average tax rate jumps to 35%, matching her new marginal rate
Her marginal rate stays at 20%, because the raise is under $5,000

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the difference between cash and in-kind transfers?

choices.text: Cash transfers go to working families; in-kind transfers go to retirees
In-kind transfers are a kind of tax; cash transfers are a public purchase
Cash transfers raise prices; in-kind transfers lower them for consumers
Cash can be spent as a family chooses; in-kind help is a specific good

questions.prompt: Two students agree on every fact about a new tax but still disagree about whether it is fair. What does this show?

choices.text: One of them has made a calculation error about the tax
Fairness can be measured exactly with the Gini coefficient
Equity involves value judgments that facts alone cannot settle
The tax is proportional, since flat taxes are widely disputed

questions.prompt: Which policy aims most directly at raising intergenerational mobility?

choices.text: Expanding early childhood education in low-income neighborhoods
Publishing a yearly index of how closely children's incomes track their parents'
Raising pensions for low-income retirees whose children are already adults
Lowering the age at which students may leave school to start working

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A district's poverty line is $20,000 a year. Three households are below it, with incomes of $14,000, $16,500, and $11,000. What is the poverty gap, the total amount needed to raise each of them exactly to the line? (Enter a number in dollars, without the $ sign or commas.)

Hypothetical example: A city wants to fund a new benefit costing $3 million a year from a flat income tax. Its taxable income base is $600 million, and assume the base does not change when the tax is introduced. Which statement is correct under a balanced budget?

choices.text: A flat tax of 5% on the base would just cover the program's cost
Borrowing the $3 million removes the cost instead of delaying it
A sales tax would take the same share of income from each household
A flat tax of 0.5% on the base would just cover the program's cost

questions.prompt: Hypothetical example: A country's official poverty measure counts only money income, such as wages and cash benefits. The government gives poor families a card that can be used only to buy groceries, and many of them now spend more on food. Other things equal, what happens to the official poverty rate?

choices.text: It falls, because the card is counted as cash income in the measure
It does not change, because in-kind help is left out of measured income
It rises, because families now spend less of their own cash on food
It falls to zero, because food needs are the basis of the poverty line
